import json
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk", font_scale=0.85)
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 120
plt.rcParams["savefig.dpi"] = 200

ROOT = Path(".")
OUT = ROOT / "outputs" / "strengthened"
FIG = OUT / "figures"
FIG.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
VERS = ROOT / "outputs" / "versions"

def savefig(name):
    p = FIG / name
    plt.savefig(p, bbox_inches="tight")
    print(f"Saved: {p}")

# Load strengthened tables
def load_csv(name):
    p = OUT / name
    if p.exists():
        return pd.read_csv(p)
    print(f"WARNING: missing {p}")
    return pd.DataFrame()

table_a = load_csv("table_a_feature_ablation_xgb.csv")
ablation_all = load_csv("feature_ablation_performance.csv")
table_b = load_csv("table_b_bootstrap_ci.csv")
table_c = load_csv("table_c_calibration.csv")
table_d = load_csv("table_d_fairness_subgroups.csv")
table_e = load_csv("table_e_faithfulness_controls.csv")
thresh = load_csv("threshold_screening_metrics.csv")
weighting = load_csv("aggregation_weighting_comparison.csv")
agg_top10 = load_csv("aggregation_top10_by_scheme.csv") if (OUT / "aggregation_top10_by_scheme.csv").exists() else pd.DataFrame()

registry = json.loads((VERS / "VERSION_REGISTRY.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if (VERS / "VERSION_REGISTRY.json").exists() else {"versions": []}
roadmap = pd.read_csv(VERS / "version_roadmap.csv") if (VERS / "version_roadmap.csv").exists() else pd.DataFrame()
rag_abl = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "outputs" / "rag_ablation_evaluation.csv") if (ROOT / "outputs" / "rag_ablation_evaluation.csv").exists() else pd.DataFrame()
perf = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "outputs" / "model_performance.csv") if (ROOT / "outputs" / "model_performance.csv").exists() else pd.DataFrame()

print("Loaded strengthened artifacts from", OUT)

2. Table A — Feature-ablation experiments (E1–E6)¶

Research question: Does the model remain useful when aca_impa (outcome-proximal) is removed?

ID Experiment
E1 Full 25 features
E2 No aca_impa
E3 No proximal MH (aca_impa, flourish, positiveMH)
E4 Social / financial / sleep only (9 features)
E5 No demographics
E6 No institution variables

if not table_a.empty:
    display(table_a.round(4))
    labels = table_a["setting"].str.replace("E1_full", "E1 Full").str.replace("E2_no_aca_impa", "E2 No aca_impa")
    labels = labels.str.replace("E3_no_proximal", "E3 No proximal").str.replace("E4_social_financial_sleep", "E4 Social/fin/sleep")
    labels = labels.str.replace("E5_no_demographics", "E5 No demo").str.replace("E6_no_institution", "E6 No inst")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
    x = np.arange(len(table_a))
    ax.bar(x, table_a["auc"], color="#4C72B0", label="AUC")
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=25, ha="right")
    ax.set_ylim(0.72, 0.88)
    ax.set_ylabel("Test AUC (XGBoost)")
    ax.set_title("Figure S1. Feature ablation — XGBoost AUC by experiment")
    for i, v in enumerate(table_a["auc"]):
        ax.text(i, v + 0.003, f"{v:.3f}", ha="center", fontsize=9)
    plt.tight_layout(); savefig("figS01_ablation_auc_xgb.png"); plt.show()

if not ablation_all.empty:
    pivot = ablation_all.pivot(index="experiment", columns="model", values="auc")
    order = ["E1_full", "E2_no_aca_impa", "E3_no_proximal", "E4_social_financial_sleep", "E5_no_demographics", "E6_no_institution"]
    pivot = pivot.reindex([e for e in order if e in pivot.index])
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
    sns.heatmap(pivot, annot=True, fmt=".3f", cmap="YlGnBu", ax=ax)
    ax.set_title("Figure S2. AUC heatmap — all ablation experiments x models")
    plt.tight_layout(); savefig("figS02_ablation_heatmap.png"); plt.show()

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5))
    for ax, col, title in zip(axes, ["auc", "pr_auc", "brier"], ["AUC", "PR-AUC", "Brier"]):
        sub = ablation_all[ablation_all.model == "XGBoost"]
        ax.bar(range(len(sub)), sub[col], color="#55A868" if col != "brier" else "#C44E52")
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(sub)))
        ax.set_xticklabels(sub["experiment"], rotation=30, ha="right", fontsize=8)
        ax.set_title(title)
    fig.suptitle("Figure S3. XGBoost metrics across ablation experiments", y=1.02)
    plt.tight_layout(); savefig("figS03_ablation_metrics_xgb.png"); plt.show()

Interpretation guide:

  • E2 drop ~0.03–0.04 AUC: model partially depends on aca_impa; still strong at ~0.82.
  • E4 AUC ~0.78 with 9 features: practical upstream screening signal without MH-proximal variables.
  • Report honestly: aca_impa is a strong marker, not an independent cause.

3. Table B — Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (XGBoost)¶

Models are tightly clustered (AUC 0.847–0.853); CIs quantify uncertainty.

In [4]:
if not table_b.empty:
    display(table_b.round(4))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
    y = table_b["metric"]
    means = table_b["mean"]
    err_lo = means - table_b["ci_low"]
    err_hi = table_b["ci_high"] - means
    ax.barh(y, means, xerr=[err_lo, err_hi], color="#4C72B0", capsize=4)
    ax.set_xlabel("Score")
    ax.set_title("Figure S4. Bootstrap 95% CI (XGBoost, test set)")
    for i, row in table_b.iterrows():
        ax.text(row["ci_high"] + 0.005, i, row["ci_95"], va="center", fontsize=9)
    plt.tight_layout(); savefig("figS04_bootstrap_ci.png"); plt.show()

4. Table C — Calibration analysis¶

In [5]:
if not table_c.empty:

# Regenerate calibration curve from saved model if available
import joblib
from sklearn.calibration import calibration_curve
from sklearn.metrics import brier_score_loss, roc_auc_score
from pipeline_common import ALL_FEATURES, load_hms_dataframe, prepare_splits, set_seeds

set_seeds()
df = load_hms_dataframe(ALL_FEATURES)
splits = prepare_splits(df, ALL_FEATURES)
y_test = splits["y_test"]
model_path = ROOT / "outputs" / "models" / "XGBoost.joblib"
if model_path.exists():
    clf = joblib.load(model_path)
    pre = joblib.load(ROOT / "outputs" / "models" / "preprocessor.joblib")
    proba = clf.predict_proba(pre.transform(splits["X_te_raw"]))[:, 1]
    prob_true, prob_pred = calibration_curve(y_test, proba, n_bins=10, strategy="uniform")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
    ax.plot(prob_pred, prob_true, "s-", color="#4C72B0", label="XGBoost")
    ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], "k--", label="Perfect calibration")
    ax.set_xlabel("Mean predicted probability")
    ax.set_ylabel("Fraction of positives")
    ax.set_title("Figure S5. Calibration reliability curve (XGBoost)")
    ax.legend()
    plt.tight_layout(); savefig("figS05_calibration_curve.png"); plt.show()
else:
    print("Saved model not found; run run_nb1.py first.")

5. Threshold-based screening metrics¶

At lower thresholds, recall increases (fewer missed high-risk students) at the cost of specificity.

In [6]:
if not thresh.empty:
    display(thresh.round(4))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    for col, label in [("recall", "Recall"), ("specificity", "Specificity"), ("precision", "Precision"), ("f1", "F1")]:
        ax.plot(thresh["threshold"], thresh[col], "o-", label=label)
    ax.set_xlabel("Classification threshold")
    ax.set_ylabel("Score")
    ax.set_title("Figure S6. Screening metrics vs threshold (XGBoost)")
    ax.legend()
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
    plt.tight_layout(); savefig("figS06_threshold_metrics.png"); plt.show()

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
    ax.plot(thresh["threshold"], thresh["fpr"], "o-", label="FPR", color="#C44E52")
    ax.plot(thresh["threshold"], thresh["fnr"], "s-", label="FNR", color="#DD8452")
    ax.set_xlabel("Threshold"); ax.set_ylabel("Rate")
    ax.set_title("Figure S7. False positive vs false negative rate")
    ax.legend()
    plt.tight_layout(); savefig("figS07_fpr_fnr.png"); plt.show()

Cross-reference from outputs/rag_ablation_evaluation.csv.

if not rag_abl.empty:
    order = ["baseline", "rag_xai", "rag_agg_xai", "full"]
    labels = {"baseline": "S0 Baseline", "rag_xai": "S1 Local XAI", "rag_agg_xai": "S2 Agg XAI", "full": "S3 Full"}
    summary = rag_abl.groupby("system")[["faithfulness", "answer_relevancy", "hallucination_rate", "context_precision", "context_recall"]].mean().reindex(order)
    summary.index = [labels.get(s, s) for s in summary.index]
    display(summary.round(3))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 6))
    summary[["faithfulness", "answer_relevancy", "hallucination_rate"]].plot.bar(ax=ax, rot=0)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1); ax.set_title("Figure S11. RAG ablation — LLM-as-judge means")
    plt.tight_layout(); savefig("figS11_rag_ablation.png"); plt.show()

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    heat = rag_abl.set_index(["case", "system"])[["faithfulness", "answer_relevancy", "hallucination_rate"]]
    heat.index = heat.index.set_levels([labels.get(l, l) for l in heat.index.levels[1]], level=1)
    sns.heatmap(heat, annot=True, fmt=".2f", cmap="RdYlGn", ax=ax, vmin=0, vmax=1)
    ax.set_title("Figure S12. RAG ablation heatmap (all cases)")

11. Key findings summary (for Discussion)¶

Finding Result
aca_impa ablation AUC drops ~0.036 without it; model still useful (~0.82)
Upstream-only (9 feat) AUC ~0.78 — practical screening without MH-proximal vars
Bootstrap CI AUC 0.853 [0.844–0.862] — models statistically tied
Calibration ECE ~0.03; consider Platt scaling
Faithfulness controls Top-5 drop >> random-5 >> bottom-5
Weighting schemes Top features robust across all schemes
RAG ablation XAI systems relevancy 0.90 vs baseline 0.77
Fairness Subgroup AUC varies; assess before deployment

Regenerate: python run_strengthened_pipeline.py then re-run this notebook.
